column6: This app understands your files with EmbeddingGemma 2, licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (the full text is below). The model files this app uses are the LiteRT-LM packages published at huggingface.co/litert-community. Changes: the models are used as published, apart from any file this app's makers fine-tuned or converted, which are marked as such. Deployments must adhere to the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy (ai.google.dev/gemma/prohibited_use_policy).

Speech recognition uses Parakeet-TDT-CTC-110M by NVIDIA, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0, creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0). Changes: it was converted to ONNX and quantised to 8-bit integers for sherpa-onnx. NVIDIA does not endorse this app.

column2: Silero VAD, by the Silero Team
column6: Finds the parts of a recording where someone is speaking. Copyright (c) 2020-present Silero Team.
Names sounds such as music, applause or a dog barking. The model, as converted for sherpa-onnx.
Stores the search index on this computer (the copy bundled with androidx.sqlite).

column2: Tesseract OCR, by the Tesseract project
column6: Linux only: reads the text in photos and screenshots by running the tesseract program you installed yourself. It is not part of this app.

On a Mac, frames and sound are read with Apple's AVFoundation, and on Windows with Media Foundation, both part of the operating system and not shipped with this app. On Linux the ffmpeg or GStreamer program you installed yourself is run when it is present; it is not part of this app.
On Windows the text in images is read with the system's own Windows.Media.Ocr, and on a Mac with Apple's Vision framework. Neither is shipped with this app.
The installer carries its own Java runtime so nothing else needs installing. It is an OpenJDK build; the Classpath Exception means it places no terms on this app's own code.
Bundled in the app's resources (from open_clip's bpe_simple_vocab_16e6.txt.gz). Copyright (c) 2021 OpenAI. The licence text is below.
Built from Webster's Second International Dictionary (1934). Tells English from other languages.
Words seen 30 or more times in the Mozilla Common Voice 17 English text corpus. No sentences are shipped.

column2: Atkinson Hyperlegible, by the Braille Institute
column6: The font this app uses, Regular and Bold. Copyright 2020 Braille Institute of America, Inc.
This app's way of combining word and meaning matches follows DigUp's design. No code was copied.

column2: Photographs in the welcome demo, from Mixkit
column6: Five small stills (birthday cake, a grandmother with her cake, a man at a party, two dogs) from Mixkit stock videos 50051, 4781, 51536, 50686 and 50672, shown in the animated demo on the first screen. The licence asks for no attribution; they are credited here anyway. Cropped and resized, not otherwise changed.

On a Mac these are opened with sips, on Windows with the imaging component (the free HEIF Image Extensions from Microsoft), on Linux with heif-convert or ImageMagick if you have installed one. None of them is shipped with this app.
